subject: MAP: performance QA flow, variant quality/perf notes & closure timeline

Subject: Re: MAP kick-off + perf validation ask

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get the MAP finalized with a hard performance validation plan before we route for budget sign-off. Specifically they want:
- TTFT and 95th latency at 8k prompt sizes for the primary call pattern
- Sustained throughput at 3 concurrency tiers (1, 16, 64) with percent-tail metrics
- One-quality gating eval against our labeled test set (500 queries) comparing top 3 Redwood variants

Can you put together a short plan and a timeline to close (we're aiming to include performance artifacts in the contract packet by 04/09)?

Helen
Head of Engineering, Edgeware Systems

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP kick-off + perf validation ask

Helen — thanks, we can cover this. High-level plan attached (redwood_map_benchmark_plan_v3). TL;DR:

Plan summary:
- Stage 1 (3 business days): run baseline latency & TTFT at 1/16/64 concurrency for the catalog variants: rwd-7b-q4, rwd-13b-fp16, rwd-13b-q4-8bit. Measurements: median, p50/p95/p99 for both server-side token latency and end-to-end TTFT.
- Stage 2 (2 business days): throughput sweep (burst and sustained) with synthetic and replayed production traces (Edgeware-provided sample).
- Stage 3 (2 business days): quality gating — run Edgeware labeled set (500) through each variant; produce accuracy/ROUGE/F1 and annotate major failure modes.
- Buffer + report (1 business day): compile results, include the performance artifact PDF for contract.

Scenario notes and tradeoffs (quick):
- rwd-7b-q4: best cost per token, good 95th latency at small context but shows higher degradation at large context under high concurrency.
- rwd-13b-fp16: best quality baseline, higher token cost and consistently higher median latency; good under batching but needs dedicated capacity for tight TTFT.
- rwd-13b-q4-8bit: sweet spot for many customers — near-13b quality at much lower memory footprint; requires a small warmup for KV cache to hit steady-state throughput.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Action: we run the Stage 1/2/3 sweep in our dedicated perf cluster.
- Deliverable: latency_results_snapshot.pdf (summary) + variant_quality_perf_matrix.csv (detailed row-level metrics) + MAP update doc.
- Proposed close checkpoint: internal sign-off by 04/06, contract packet ready 04/09.

I'll start the runs today once we get the sanitized sample trace from you (safe to drop to the Drive link in my related_links).

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: MAP kick-off + perf validation ask

Thanks team — results attached from the internal runs we kicked off last week. Notes below; see variant_quality_perf_matrix.csv for per-query rows.

Executive highlights:
- TTFT (8k prompt, 1 concurrent): rwd-13b-fp16 median 420ms, p95 980ms. rwd-13b-q4-8bit median 310ms, p95 860ms. rwd-7b-q4 median 190ms, p95 590ms.
- Sustained throughput (64 concurrent, 8k prompt): rwd-13b-fp16 55 tok/s sustained, rwd-13b-q4-8bit 72 tok/s, rwd-7b-q4 95 tok/s — note these include 10% exec overhead from the KV warmup window.
- Quality gating (Edgeware 500 queries): rwd-13b-fp16 highest micro-F1 (0.82), rwd-13b-q4-8bit (0.79), rwd-7b-q4 (0.68). Failure modes for 7b: hallucinations on multi-step instructions; for q4-8bit: occasional truncation on very long outputs ~>6k tokens if cache isn't primed.

Tradeoff recommendation for Edgeware use case (real-time documentation summarization with prioritized safety filters):
- If strict quality baseline required for contract, rwd-13b-fp16 is recommended with Dedicated S2-X and higher reserve.
- If cost sensitivity and 95th latency objective at scale is priority, rwd-13b-q4-8bit is the recommended compromise.
- rwd-7b-q4 is acceptable for low-cost prototypes or background batch jobs, not for front-line user-facing flows.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Edgeware confirms whether the p95 latency in the artifact is acceptable for the contract.
2) Procurement confirms which variant(s) they want modeled in the cost appendix.
3) We schedule a short review with engineering (30m) to walk the detailed CSV results — proposed 04/01 or 04/02.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: variant_quality_perf_matrix.csv (csv, 210 KB), latency_results_snapshot.pdf (pdf, 48 KB)]
